front.title: Post-Quantum Secure Transport (PQST): Overview and Reading Guide

abstract.t: PQST (Post-Quantum Secure Transport) is a post-quantum native session-primary datagram transport for secure tunnels without classical public key cryptography, hybrid key exchange, or classical fallback. The cryptographic session is the persistent object, the network path is a replaceable carrier, and a session can be re- anchored on a new path, after a restart, or after the loss of every path, with fresh post-quantum key material and without the session, its authorization, or the peers' authenticated identities changing. The cohort layer of PQST applies the same idea one level up: a group whose members' sessions move, sleep, recover and re-key independently while the group's membership changes only on security events. This document is a non-normative overview of, and reading guide to, the specifications of those two layers. It defines no wire format, no behaviour, and no requirements. The core protocol is proposed as the basis for Standards Track work; the cohort layer is Experimental. The author is seeking a working-group home for the core protocol and implementation experience with both layers.
